To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the quality of studies examining donor biopsies was generally low, that biopsy findings were not consistently associated with outcomes, and that there was a lack of consistency in the methods and results of these studies.

(1) the majority of studies examining the association between donor kidney biopsies and post-transplant outcomes are retrospective, (2) the majority of donor kidneys are discarded because of biopsy results, (3) the majority of the studies that examined the association did not find a statistically significant association between donor kidney biopsy results and post-transplant graft failure, (4) the majority of these studies were not designed to determine if donor kidney biopsy results predict post-transplant graft function, and (5)

the quality of the evidence on the predictive value of donor kidney biopsy findings for posttransplant outcomes is poor, and that biopsy findings do not predict posttransplanted graft failure, delayed function, or function.

the current literature does not support a strong association between donor kidney biopsy findings and posttransplant outcomes and that more rigorous research is required to better understand the utility of donor kidney biopsies.
